title: Ripple is preparing XRP Ledger for quantum computers before ‘Q-Day’ arrives
summary: An Anthropic model cut the work needed to break a leading post-quantum signature candidate by a factor of 67 million last month, while Bitcoin and Ethereum published their own migration plans this week.
content: Ripple is proactively preparing the XRP Ledger for future quantum computing threats ahead of potential risks. This follows recent developments where an advanced model significantly reduced the computational work required to break a leading post-quantum signature candidate. Meanwhile, major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum have also published their own migration plans to address these upcoming technological challenges this week.

title: How Bitcoin is drifting away from tech stocks… and straight into gold’s territory!
summary: Binance's Changpeng Zhao says Bitcoin could overtake gold soon.
content: Recent commentary highlights a shifting perception of Bitcoin in financial markets. Rather than continuing to track closely with technology stocks, cryptocurrency observers note that Bitcoin is increasingly behaving more like a traditional safe-haven asset, drawing comparisons to gold. Leadership at Binance has suggested that Bitcoin could potentially rival or surpass gold in the near future as its market role evolves.

title: CFTC Signals Supreme Court Battle After Nevada Wins Prediction Markets Case
summary:
A court’s ruling that sports event contracts are not swaps that are regulated exclusively by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) set the stage for a Supreme Court case, a CFTC spokesperson told PYMNTS Friday (Aug. 28). The statement came after a Friday ruling in a court battle between Nevada and three companies offering prediction markets. […]
The post CFTC Signals Supreme Court Battle After Nevada Wins Prediction Markets Case appeared first on PYMNTS.com.
content: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has indicated it may take a prediction markets dispute to the Supreme Court. This follows a court ruling that sports event contracts are not swaps regulated exclusively by the agency. The legal battle involves Nevada and three prediction market companies, setting the stage for a potential high-court showdown over regulatory jurisdiction.
